newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open mostly flat Thursday as concerns over frost-damage to Brazil's coffee crop have subsided, dealers said.

Weather Services Corp forecast below normal temperatures in parts of Brazil this weekend but said there is no damaging cold weather expected for the next seven days. Scattered showers and thunderstorms could develop in northern Parana today, while light showers could hit Sao Paulo and Minas Gerias over the weekend, WSC said.
Some traders said prices could climb higher during the session in a retracement of recent losses.
Wednesday, CSCE benchmark September closed 2.90 cents lower at 172.35 cents per lb. Scale-down roaster buying supported the contract over its downside target of 169-167 cents.
On the upside, resistance was seen near 184.50-185.00 cents, followed by 192.00.
Following the close of business on Wednesday, CSCE reported an additional 55,000 bags awaiting grading in exchange warehouses. The total number of bags stands at 82,000.
CSCE will be closed on Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
London robusta futures firmed slightly by midday Thursday but September remained below the session high. At the break, the key month stood $10 higher at $1,850.
